item.title: Centre issues Directions to protect Aravalli Range and ban mining leases
item.description: Govt issues directions to protect Aravalli Range, imposing a ban on new mining leases and planning sustainable management to ensure ecological balance and stronger environmental governance. The post Centre issues Directions to protect Aravalli Range and ban mining leases appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: “Not a case of Sexual Harassment”: Allahabad High Court remits MNNIT Lecturer’s “shockingly disproportionate” dismissal for Consensual Relationship with ex-student
item.description: In the case at hand, a written complaint was filed by an ex-student of Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology, Allahabad alleging that during her Masters, a Lecturer had established a physical relationship with her against her will. The post “Not a case of Sexual Harassment”: Allahabad High Court remits MNNIT Lecturer’s “shockingly disproportionate” dismissal for Consensual Relationship with ex-student appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Non-compete fee: Revenue or capital expenditure? Supreme Court explains
item.description: “Non-compete fee only seeks to protect or enhance the profitability of the business, thereby facilitating the carrying on of the business more efficiently and profitably.” The post Non-compete fee: Revenue or capital expenditure? Supreme Court explains appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Civil suit cannot vitiate arbitral awards on grounds of fraud: Delhi High Court upholds Single Judge’s order
item.description: Once arbitral award attains finality up to the Supreme Court, separate civil suit challenging underlying transaction on grounds of fraud is barred by Section 5 of the Arbitration Act and principles of finality. The post Civil suit cannot vitiate arbitral awards on grounds of fraud: Delhi High Court upholds Single Judge’s order appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Mere Reference to Caste Name Not an Offence Unless Used to Intentionally Insult or Humiliate: Bombay High Court Quashes FIR Against Marathi TV Channel Executives
item.description: No specific allegation was made that the petitioners, who were not members of a scheduled caste or scheduled tribe, had intentionally undertaken an act to insult, intimidate or humiliate the first informant, who is a member of the scheduled caste. The post Mere Reference to Caste Name Not an Offence Unless Used to Intentionally Insult or Humiliate: Bombay High Court Quashes FIR Against Marathi TV Channel Executives appeared first on SCC Times.
